public_rationale: GitHub's announcement dated April 20, 2026 confirmed plans to pause new Student, Pro and Pro+ signups [e1]. Its community announcement, updated April 24, explicitly confirmed tighter individual-plan usage limits [e2]. ITPro's April 28 report quoted GitHub's product chief describing the previous week's restrictions as preparation for a broader transition to usage-based billing, supporting that the transition was already planned [e3].
limitations: The evidence does not independently authenticate the leaked documents.
The quoted passage in e3 establishes a connection to usage-based billing but does not specify token consumption or model prices.
The evidence does not establish that customer charges equal Microsoft's internal compute costs.
The connection between the April restrictions and the billing-transition plan rests on the retrospective explanation reported by ITPro [e3].

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Leaked documents show Microsoft plans to pause new student and paid individual GitHub Copilot signups, tighten rate limits, and eventually move users to token-based billing.

statement.excerpt: Leaked internal documents viewed by Where’s Your Ed At reveal that Microsoft intends to pause new signups for the student and paid individual tiers of AI coding product GitHub Copilot, tighter rate limits, and eventually move users to “token-based billing,” charging them based on what the actual cost of their token burn really is.
statement.document_title: Exclusive: Microsoft To Shift GitHub Copilot Users To Token-Based Billing, Tighten Rate Limits

from_speaker: pause new signups for the student and paid individual tiers
actual cost of their token burn
our_interpretation: Assess whether Microsoft held the three stated policy plans on April 20, 2026, rather than treating eventual implementation as a forecast with an invented deadline.
Paid individual tiers means Pro and Pro+, as specified in the surrounding text.

Read token-based billing as charging according to token consumption and model prices. The surrounding API-price example indicates retail token charges, not verified reimbursement of Microsoft's internal costs.
Later statements count as evidence of April intent only when they explicitly describe the earlier restrictions as preparation for the billing transition.
The assessment addresses the substance of the plans, not independent authentication of the leaked documents.
criteria.support_condition: Dated company statements or reliable reporting of those statements establish the signup pause, tighter usage limits, and an already-planned transition to token-based billing.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Reliable contemporaneous records establish that a material stated plan did not exist, was misreported, or concerned different subscription tiers.
